records.source: וַיְהִ֣י׀בַּחֹ֣דֶשׁ הַשְּׁבִיעִ֗י בָּ֣א יִשְׁמָעֵ֣אל בֶּן־נְתַנְיָ֣ה בֶן־אֱלִישָׁמָ֣ע מִזֶּ֣רַע הַ֠מְּלוּכָה וְרַבֵּ֨י הַמֶּ֜לֶךְ וַעֲשָׂרָ֨ה אֲנָשִׁ֥ים אִתּ֛וֹ אֶל־גְּדַלְיָ֥הוּ בֶן־אֲחִיקָ֖ם הַמִּצְפָּ֑תָה וַיֹּ֨אכְלוּ שָׁ֥ם לֶ֛חֶם יַחְדָּ֖ו בַּמִּצְפָּֽה׃
records.gloss: And it was in the month the seventh, came Ishmael son of Nethaniah son of Elishama, of [the] seed of the kingship, and [the] chiefs of the king, and ten men with him, to Gedaliah son of Ahikam [to] Mizpah, and they ate there bread together at Mizpah.
pieces: In the seventh month Ishmael son of Nethaniah, son of Elishama, who was of royal descent and one of the king's chief officers, came to Gedaliah son of Ahikam at Mizpah, bringing ten men with him. There at Mizpah they ate a meal together.

L.1: And it came about in the seventh month [that] Ishmael son of Nethaniah son of Elishama, of the royal seed and [one of] the chief officers of the king, came, and ten men with him, to Gedaliah son of Ahikam at Mizpah, and they ate bread there together at Mizpah.

R.1: In the seventh month, Ishmael son of Nethaniah and grandson of Elishama came to Gedaliah son of Ahikam at Mizpah with ten men. Ishmael belonged to the royal family and was one of the king's high officers. They all ate a meal together there at Mizpah.

decisions.choice: told briefly in 2 Kings 25:25
decisions.reason: 2 Kings 25:25 tells the same murder in one verse. Jeremiah adds three things: that Ishmael was also one of the king's chief officers, the name of Gedaliah's father, and the meal they shared before the killing. Kings says only that Ishmael and his men came and struck Gedaliah down.

decisions.choice: the seventh month: autumn; no year is given
decisions.reason: As in 2 Kings 25:25, the year is not named. It is usually taken to be the same year that Jerusalem fell, about two months after the temple was burned (52:12-13), but it may have been a later year.

decisions.choice: and [one of] the chief officers of the king: a second description of Ishmael
alternatives: some of the king's chief officers came with him
decisions.reason: The words are loosely joined to what comes before. They can describe Ishmael himself, as a man of the royal line who also held high rank at court, or they can name a further group who came with him, some of the king's officers. 2 Kings 25:25 does not have the phrase, and the Greek translation is reported not to have it either, which suggests it may be a later addition to the Hebrew. The first reading fits the singular verb "came".

decisions.choice: they ate bread together: a shared meal, a bond of trust
decisions.reason: To eat at someone's table was to be his guest and under his protection. Killing a host after sharing his food was a deep betrayal (Psalm 41:10). Gedaliah had been warned that Ishmael meant to kill him and had refused to believe it (40:13-16).

decisions.choice: of the royal seed (Literal); of royal descent (Balanced); a member of the royal family (Readable); a meal (Balanced and Readable)
decisions.reason: Worded as in 2 Kings 25:25. "Bread" stands for food in general, so Balanced and Readable say "a meal". Readable gives Ishmael's rank in a sentence of its own.

records.heading: Ishmael kills Gedaliah

records.source: וַיָּקָם֩ יִשְׁמָעֵ֨אל בֶּן־נְתַנְיָ֜ה וַעֲשֶׂ֥רֶת הָאֲנָשִׁ֣ים׀אֲשֶׁר־הָי֣וּ אִתּ֗וֹ וַ֠יַּכּוּ אֶת־גְּדַלְיָ֨הוּ בֶן־אֲחִיקָ֧ם בֶּן־שָׁפָ֛ן בַּחֶ֖רֶב וַיָּ֣מֶת אֹת֑וֹ אֲשֶׁר־הִפְקִ֥יד מֶֽלֶךְ־בָּבֶ֖ל בָּאָֽרֶץ׃
records.gloss: And arose Ishmael son of Nethaniah and the ten men who were with him, and they struck Gedaliah son of Ahikam son of Shaphan with the sword, and he put to death him whom had appointed [the] king of Babylon over the land.
pieces: Then Ishmael son of Nethaniah and the ten men with him got up and struck down Gedaliah son of Ahikam, son of Shaphan, with the sword. So he killed the man whom the king of Babylon had appointed governor of the land.

L.2: And Ishmael son of Nethaniah and the ten men who were with him arose and struck Gedaliah son of Ahikam son of Shaphan with the sword, and he put to death him whom the king of Babylon had appointed over the land.

R.2: Then Ishmael son of Nethaniah and the ten men with him got up and attacked Gedaliah son of Ahikam, the son of Shaphan, with their swords. So Ishmael killed the man the king of Babylon had put in charge of the land.

decisions.choice: they struck ... he put to death: the band attacked, and Ishmael is held responsible
decisions.reason: The first verb is plural, for Ishmael and his ten men; the second is singular. The killing is laid to Ishmael as the leader, as again in verses 16 and 18.

decisions.choice: whom the king of Babylon had appointed over the land: the governor
decisions.reason: The narrator names Gedaliah by his office here and again in verse 18. Killing the man Babylon had set over the land was rebellion against Babylon, which is why the survivors feared reprisal (verse 18; 40:5, 7).

decisions.choice: appointed governor of (Balanced); put in charge of (Readable); with their swords (Readable)
decisions.reason: As in 2 Kings 25:22, Balanced names the office and Readable says what it was. The Hebrew says "with the sword", meaning swords as weapons; Readable makes it plain that the men used their own.

records.source: וְאֵ֣ת כָּל־הַיְּהוּדִ֗ים אֲשֶׁר־הָי֨וּ אִתּ֤וֹ אֶת־גְּדַלְיָ֨הוּ֙ בַּמִּצְפָּ֔ה וְאֶת־הַכַּשְׂדִּ֖ים אֲשֶׁ֣ר נִמְצְאוּ־שָׁ֑ם אֵ֚ת אַנְשֵׁ֣י הַמִּלְחָמָ֔ה הִכָּ֖ה יִשְׁמָעֵֽאל׃
records.gloss: And all the Judeans who were with him, with Gedaliah, in Mizpah, and the Chaldeans who were found there, the men of the war, struck Ishmael.
pieces: Ishmael also struck down all the Judeans who were with Gedaliah at Mizpah, and the Chaldean soldiers who happened to be there.

L.3: And all the Judeans who were with him, with Gedaliah, at Mizpah, and the Chaldeans who were found there, the men of war, Ishmael struck down.

R.3: Ishmael also killed all the people of Judah who were with Gedaliah at Mizpah. He killed the Babylonian soldiers who were there too.

decisions.choice: the Chaldeans ..., the men of war: the Babylonian soldiers
decisions.reason: "The men of war" follows the Chaldeans with no "and", so it says who they were: soldiers stationed at Mizpah. It is not a third group of Judean soldiers, for some Judean fighting men were still alive afterward (verse 16).

decisions.choice: all the Judeans who were with him: those in Gedaliah's company
decisions.reason: "All" means the people with Gedaliah at the time, his household and attendants. Many other people of Judah remained in Mizpah, and Ishmael took them captive (verse 10).

decisions.choice: as 2 Kings 25:25, which does not say they were soldiers
decisions.reason: 2 Kings 25:25 names "the Judeans and the Chaldeans who were with him at Mizpah". Jeremiah adds that the Chaldeans were men of war who happened to be there.

decisions.choice: Ishmael ... struck down (Balanced); Ishmael also killed (Readable); people of Judah, Babylonian (Readable)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew puts the victims first and the subject and verb last, for emphasis; Literal keeps that order. Balanced and Readable start with Ishmael. Readable says "people of Judah" for Judeans and "Babylonian" for Chaldean, as in Isaiah.

records.source: וַיְהִ֛י בַּיּ֥וֹם הַשֵּׁנִ֖י לְהָמִ֣ית אֶת־גְּדַלְיָ֑הוּ וְאִ֖ישׁ לֹ֥א יָדָֽע׃
records.gloss: And it was on the day the second after putting to death Gedaliah, and a man not knew,
pieces: On the day after Gedaliah's murder, before anyone knew about it,

L.4: And it came about on the second day after he had put Gedaliah to death, and no one knew [it],

R.4: The day after Gedaliah was killed, no one knew about it yet.

decisions.choice: the second day: the next day
decisions.reason: Counting the day of the murder as the first, "the second day" is the day after it.

decisions.choice: and no one knew: the murder was still a secret
decisions.reason: This clause describes the situation: no one outside had yet heard what had happened. It explains how the men in the next verse could walk into Mizpah unwarned.

decisions.choice: a sentence of its own (Readable)
decisions.reason: Literal and Balanced end with a comma, because the sentence runs on into verse 5. Readable makes this verse a sentence by itself.

records.source: וַיָּבֹ֣אוּ אֲ֠נָשִׁים מִשְּׁכֶ֞ם מִשִּׁל֤וֹ וּמִשֹּֽׁמְרוֹן֙ שְׁמֹנִ֣ים אִ֔ישׁ מְגֻלְּחֵ֥י זָקָ֛ן וּקְרֻעֵ֥י בְגָדִ֖ים וּמִתְגֹּֽדְדִ֑ים וּמִנְחָ֤ה וּלְבוֹנָה֙ בְּיָדָ֔ם לְהָבִ֖יא בֵּ֥ית יְהוָֽה׃
records.gloss: and came men from Shechem, from Shiloh, and from Samaria, eighty man, shaven of beard and torn of clothes and cutting themselves, and grain offering and frankincense in their hand to bring [to the] house of Yahweh.
pieces: eighty men arrived from Shechem, Shiloh and Samaria. Their beards were shaved, their clothes torn and their bodies gashed, and they were carrying grain offerings and frankincense to bring to the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

L.5: and men came from Shechem, from Shiloh and from Samaria, eighty men, with beards shaved and clothes torn and gashing themselves, and [with] grain offering and frankincense in their hand to bring [to] the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

R.5: Eighty men came from the towns of Shechem, Shiloh and Samaria. They had shaved off their beards, torn their clothes and cut their skin to show their grief. They were carrying grain offerings and incense to offer at the temple of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: Shechem, Shiloh and Samaria: towns of the former northern kingdom
decisions.reason: All three lay in the old territory of Israel to the north, which Assyria had conquered long before (2 Kings 17:5-6). Some people there still came to worship the LORD at Jerusalem (2 Chronicles 30:11; 34:9).

decisions.choice: shaved beards, torn clothes and gashed bodies: signs of mourning
decisions.reason: These were the customs of grief in that world (16:6; 47:5; 48:37). The law forbade gashing the body for the dead (Leviticus 19:28; Deuteronomy 14:1), but the practice went on. The men were most likely mourning the fall of Jerusalem and the burning of the temple.

decisions.choice: grain offering and frankincense for the house of the LORD: gifts brought to the ruined temple
alternatives: a place of worship at Mizpah
decisions.reason: The temple had been burned (52:13), yet these men were still bringing offerings to the place where it had stood. They bring grain and frankincense, not animals for sacrifice. Some think "the house of the LORD" here means a place of worship at Mizpah, but the phrase usually means the temple in Jerusalem, and Mizpah lay on the road there from the north.

decisions.choice: to show their grief; incense (Readable)
decisions.reason: Readable says why the men had done these things (m2) and uses the plain word "incense" for frankincense.

decisions.choice: eighty men arrived (Balanced); a new sentence (Readable)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew gives the places first and the number after. Balanced and Readable put the number first and describe the men in a sentence of their own.

records.source: וַ֠יֵּצֵא יִשְׁמָעֵ֨אל בֶּן־נְתַנְיָ֤ה לִקְרָאתָם֙ מִן־הַמִּצְפָּ֔ה הֹלֵ֥ךְ הָלֹ֖ךְ וּבֹכֶ֑ה וַֽיְהִי֙ כִּפְגֹ֣שׁ אֹתָ֔ם וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֲלֵיהֶ֔ם בֹּ֖אוּ אֶל־גְּדַלְיָ֥הוּ בֶן־אֲחִיקָֽם׃ס
records.gloss: And went out Ishmael son of Nethaniah to meet them from Mizpah, going going and weeping; and it was as meeting them, and he said to them, Come to Gedaliah son of Ahikam.
pieces: Ishmael son of Nethaniah left Mizpah to meet them, weeping as he went along. When he met them, he said to them, "Come to Gedaliah son of Ahikam."

L.6: And Ishmael son of Nethaniah went out from Mizpah to meet them, going along and weeping; and it came about, as he met them, [that] he said to them, "Come to Gedaliah son of Ahikam."

R.6: Ishmael son of Nethaniah went out from Mizpah to meet them. He cried as he walked along. When he met them, he said, "Come and see Gedaliah son of Ahikam."

decisions.choice: going along and weeping: Ishmael wept all the way
alternatives: the eighty men were weeping as they went
decisions.reason: The repeated verb "going, going" shows action that goes on, and "weeping" goes with it. The Greek translation is reported to say that the men were the ones weeping; the Hebrew says it of Ishmael.

decisions.choice: his weeping and his invitation: a deception
decisions.reason: Ishmael pretended to share their grief, and he invited them to the governor, hiding that Gedaliah was already dead. Both were meant to lead them into the town without suspicion.

decisions.choice: Come and see (Readable)
decisions.reason: "Come to Gedaliah" invites them to visit him. Readable says it in everyday words.

records.source: וַיְהִ֕י כְּבוֹאָ֖ם אֶל־תּ֣וֹךְ הָעִ֑יר וַיִּשְׁחָטֵ֞ם יִשְׁמָעֵ֤אל בֶּן־נְתַנְיָה֙ אֶל־תּ֣וֹךְ הַבּ֔וֹר ה֖וּא וְהָאֲנָשִׁ֥ים אֲשֶׁר־אִתּֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: And it was as their coming into [the] midst of the city, and slaughtered them Ishmael son of Nethaniah into [the] midst of the cistern, he and the men who [were] with him.
pieces: But as soon as they were inside the city, Ishmael son of Nethaniah and his men slaughtered them and threw them into the cistern.

L.7: And it came about, when they came into the middle of the city, [that] Ishmael son of Nethaniah slaughtered them [and threw them] into the middle of the cistern, he and the men who [were] with him.

R.7: But as soon as they were inside the town, Ishmael and his men killed them. They threw the bodies into a cistern, a pit dug to hold water.

decisions.choice: slaughtered them into the cistern: killed them and threw them in
decisions.reason: The Hebrew joins the killing and the place the bodies ended up in one short phrase. Verse 9 says plainly that Ishmael threw the bodies into the cistern.

decisions.choice: slaughtered: killed like animals
decisions.reason: The verb is the one used for slaughtering animals, often for sacrifice. Men who had come to bring offerings were themselves butchered.

decisions.choice: he and the men who were with him: his ten men shared in it
decisions.reason: The words come at the end of the sentence and add Ishmael's band to the deed.

decisions.choice: [and threw them] (Literal); and threw them (Balanced); They threw the bodies into a cistern, a pit dug to hold water (Readable)
decisions.reason: English needs a verb for the bodies going into the cistern (m1). Readable explains what a cistern is. Readable shortens Ishmael's name, which is given in full just before.

records.source: וַעֲשָׂרָ֨ה אֲנָשִׁ֜ים נִמְצְאוּ־בָ֗ם וַיֹּאמְר֤וּ אֶל־יִשְׁמָעֵאל֙ אַל־תְּמִתֵ֔נוּ כִּֽי־יֶשׁ־לָ֤נוּ מַטְמֹנִים֙ בַּשָּׂדֶ֔ה חִטִּ֥ים וּשְׂעֹרִ֖ים וְשֶׁ֣מֶן וּדְבָ֑שׁ וַיֶּחְדַּ֕ל וְלֹ֥א הֱמִיתָ֖ם בְּת֥וֹךְ אֲחֵיהֶֽם׃
records.gloss: And ten men were found among them, and they said to Ishmael, Do not kill us, for there are to us hidden stores in the field, wheat and barley and oil and honey; and he refrained and not killed them in [the] midst of their brothers.
pieces: But there were ten men among them who said to Ishmael, "Do not kill us! We have stores of wheat, barley, oil and honey hidden in the countryside." So he held back and did not kill them along with their companions.

L.8: And ten men were found among them, and they said to Ishmael, "Do not kill us, for we have hidden stores in the field: wheat and barley and oil and honey." And he refrained and did not kill them among their brothers.

R.8: But ten of the men said to Ishmael, "Do not kill us! We have wheat, barley, olive oil and honey hidden out in the fields." So Ishmael let them live and did not kill them with the others.

decisions.choice: hidden stores in the field: food buried for safe keeping
decisions.reason: Grain, oil and honey were kept in pits and jars hidden in the open country, out of reach of raiders. After war and siege, food was precious, and the ten men bought their lives with it.

decisions.choice: their brothers: their companions
decisions.reason: "Brothers" here means the other men in their group, their fellow countrymen.

decisions.choice: honey: perhaps a syrup made from fruit
decisions.reason: The word can mean bees' honey or a thick syrup from dates or grapes. Either fits a store of food.

decisions.choice: countryside (Balanced); out in the fields, olive oil, let them live, the others (Readable); companions (Balanced)
decisions.reason: "Field" means open country outside the town. Readable names the kind of oil and says plainly what "refrained" meant for the ten men.

records.source: וְהַבּ֗וֹר אֲשֶׁר֩ הִשְׁלִ֨יךְ שָׁ֤ם יִשְׁמָעֵאל֙ אֵ֣ת׀כָּל־פִּגְרֵ֣י הָאֲנָשִׁ֗ים אֲשֶׁ֤ר הִכָּה֙ בְּיַד־גְּדַלְיָ֔הוּ ה֗וּא אֲשֶׁ֤ר עָשָׂה֙ הַמֶּ֣לֶךְ אָסָ֔א מִפְּנֵ֖י בַּעְשָׁ֣א מֶֽלֶךְ־יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל אֹת֗וֹ מִלֵּ֛א יִשְׁמָעֵ֥אל בֶּן־נְתַנְיָ֖הוּ חֲלָלִֽים׃
records.gloss: And the cistern where threw there Ishmael all [the] corpses of the men whom he struck by [the] hand of Gedaliah, it [was] which made the king Asa from [the] face of Baasha king of Israel; it filled Ishmael son of Nethaniah [with the] slain.
pieces: The cistern where Ishmael threw the bodies of all the men he had struck down along with Gedaliah was the one King Asa had made for defense against Baasha king of Israel. Ishmael son of Nethaniah filled it with those he had killed.

L.9: And the cistern where Ishmael threw all the corpses of the men whom he had struck down by the hand of Gedaliah, it [was the one] that King Asa had made because of Baasha king of Israel; Ishmael son of Nethaniah filled it [with the] slain.

R.9: Ishmael threw the bodies of all the men he had killed along with Gedaliah into a cistern. King Asa had made it long before, when he was afraid of an attack by Baasha king of Israel. Ishmael son of Nethaniah filled it with dead bodies.

decisions.choice: by the hand of Gedaliah: along with Gedaliah
alternatives: by means of Gedaliah, using his name
decisions.reason: The Hebrew phrase is hard to explain here. It may mean "beside Gedaliah", that is, along with him, or "by means of Gedaliah", because Ishmael lured the men in by using the governor's name (verse 6). The Greek translation is reported to read instead "it was a great cistern", which would come from a Hebrew text with very similar letters. The Hebrew text is kept, in the first sense.

decisions.choice: the cistern King Asa made because of Baasha
decisions.reason: Asa king of Judah and Baasha king of Israel were at war, and Asa fortified Geba and Mizpah against him (1 Kings 15:16-22; 2 Chronicles 16:1-6). Those passages do not mention a cistern, but a great cistern would have kept the town supplied with water in a siege. This one was about three hundred years old.

decisions.choice: filled it with slain: the number of the dead
decisions.reason: The cistern was large, and Ishmael filled it with the bodies of those he had killed.

decisions.choice: for defense against (Balanced); long before, when he was afraid of an attack by (Readable)
decisions.reason: "From the face of Baasha" means because of the threat Baasha posed. Balanced and Readable say so.

decisions.choice: along with Gedaliah
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable follow the first sense in m1. Literal keeps the Hebrew phrase as it stands.

records.source: וַיִּ֣שְׁבְּ׀יִ֠שְׁמָעֵאל אֶת־כָּל־שְׁאֵרִ֨ית הָעָ֜ם אֲשֶׁ֣ר בַּמִּצְפָּ֗ה אֶת־בְּנ֤וֹת הַמֶּ֨לֶךְ֙ וְאֶת־כָּל־הָעָם֙ הַנִּשְׁאָרִ֣ים בַּמִּצְפָּ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֣ר הִפְקִ֗יד נְבֽוּזַרְאֲדָן֙ רַב־טַבָּחִ֔ים אֶת־גְּדַלְיָ֖הוּ בֶּן־אֲחִיקָ֑ם וַיִּשְׁבֵּם֙ יִשְׁמָעֵ֣אל בֶּן־נְתַנְיָ֔ה וַיֵּ֕לֶךְ לַעֲבֹ֖ר אֶל־בְּנֵ֥י עַמּֽוֹן׃ס
records.gloss: And took captive Ishmael all [the] rest of the people who [were] in Mizpah, the daughters of the king and all the people remaining in Mizpah, whom had appointed Nebuzaradan chief of [the] guards [to] Gedaliah son of Ahikam; and took them captive Ishmael son of Nethaniah, and he went to cross over to [the] sons of Ammon.
pieces: Ishmael took captive all the rest of the people who were at Mizpah: the king's daughters and all the others left at Mizpah, whom Nebuzaradan the captain of the guard had placed in the care of Gedaliah son of Ahikam. Ishmael son of Nethaniah carried them off as captives and set out to cross over to the Ammonites.

L.10: And Ishmael took captive all the rest of the people who [were] at Mizpah, the daughters of the king and all the people who remained at Mizpah, whom Nebuzaradan the chief of the guard had committed to Gedaliah son of Ahikam; and Ishmael son of Nethaniah took them captive and went to cross over to the {{gender:children|sons}} of Ammon.

R.10: Then Ishmael captured all the other people at Mizpah. Among them were the king's daughters and everyone else who had been left at Mizpah. Nebuzaradan, the commander of the royal guard, had put them in Gedaliah's care. Ishmael son of Nethaniah took them as prisoners and set out to cross over to the land of the Ammonites.

decisions.choice: the daughters of the king: women of the royal house
decisions.reason: These were probably daughters of King Zedekiah, or women of the royal family more widely. They are named again among those taken to Egypt (43:6).

decisions.choice: whom Nebuzaradan had appointed to Gedaliah: placed in his charge
decisions.reason: The verb used for appointing an official here means handing people over to someone's care. Nebuzaradan had left the poorest people of the land and these others under Gedaliah's rule (39:10; 40:7).

decisions.choice: to cross over to the Ammonites: east of the Jordan
decisions.reason: Ammon lay across the Jordan to the east. Baalis king of the Ammonites had sent Ishmael to kill Gedaliah (40:14), so Ishmael was heading back to his protector.

decisions.choice: the chief of the guard (Literal); the captain of the guard (Balanced); the commander of the royal guard (Readable); the Ammonites (Balanced and Readable)
decisions.reason: Nebuzaradan's title is worded as in 2 Kings 25:8. "The sons of Ammon" is the people of Ammon; Literal uses the gender setting, as elsewhere in Jeremiah. Readable adds "the land of" because the Ammonites were a people living in a land of their own.

records.source: וַיִּשְׁמַע֙ יוֹחָנָ֣ן בֶּן־קָרֵ֔חַ וְכָל־שָׂרֵ֥י הַחֲיָלִ֖ים אֲשֶׁ֣ר אִתּ֑וֹ אֵ֤ת כָּל־הָֽרָעָה֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשָׂ֔ה יִשְׁמָעֵ֖אל בֶּן־נְתַנְיָֽה׃
records.gloss: And heard Johanan son of Kareah and all [the] commanders of the forces who [were] with him all the evil which had done Ishmael son of Nethaniah,
pieces: When Johanan son of Kareah and all the commanders of the forces with him heard of all the evil Ishmael son of Nethaniah had done,

L.11: And Johanan son of Kareah and all the commanders of the forces who [were] with him heard [of] all the evil that Ishmael son of Nethaniah had done,

R.11: Johanan son of Kareah and all the army commanders with him heard about all the evil things Ishmael son of Nethaniah had done.

decisions.choice: the evil: his crimes
decisions.reason: "Evil" here is the wrong Ishmael had done: the murders and the taking of captives.

decisions.choice: Johanan had warned Gedaliah
decisions.reason: Johanan and the other commanders had told Gedaliah that Ishmael was sent to kill him, and Johanan had offered to kill Ishmael first (40:13-16).

decisions.choice: a sentence of its own (Readable); army commanders (Readable)
decisions.reason: Literal and Balanced end with a comma, as the sentence goes on into verse 12. Readable makes the verse a sentence and says "army commanders", as in 2 Kings 25:23.

records.heading: Johanan brings the captives back

records.source: וַיִּקְחוּ֙ אֶת־כָּל־הָ֣אֲנָשִׁ֔ים וַיֵּ֣לְכ֔וּ לְהִלָּחֵ֖ם עִם־יִשְׁמָעֵ֣אל בֶּן־נְתַנְיָ֑ה וַיִּמְצְא֣וּ אֹת֔וֹ אֶל־מַ֥יִם רַבִּ֖ים אֲשֶׁ֥ר בְּגִבְעֽוֹן׃
records.gloss: and they took all the men and went to fight with Ishmael son of Nethaniah, and they found him at [the] waters [the] great which [are] in Gibeon.
pieces: they took all their men and went to fight against Ishmael son of Nethaniah. They found him by the great pool in Gibeon.

L.12: and they took all the men and went to fight with Ishmael son of Nethaniah, and they found him by the great waters that [are] in Gibeon.

R.12: So they took all their men and set out to fight Ishmael son of Nethaniah. They caught up with him near the large pool at Gibeon.

decisions.choice: the great waters: a large pool
decisions.reason: This was the pool or reservoir of Gibeon, where the men of David and of Ishbosheth once met (2 Samuel 2:13).

decisions.choice: Gibeon: a town near Mizpah
decisions.reason: Gibeon lay a few miles from Mizpah in the land of Benjamin. Ishmael and his captives had not got far.

decisions.choice: their men; pool (Balanced and Readable); caught up with (Readable)
decisions.reason: "All the men" are the commanders' own men. Balanced and Readable name the great waters as a pool (m1), and Readable says that finding Ishmael meant catching up with him.

records.source: וַיְהִ֗י כִּרְא֤וֹת כָּל־הָעָם֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר אֶת־יִשְׁמָעֵ֔אל אֶת־יֽוֹחָנָן֙ בֶּן־קָרֵ֔חַ וְאֵ֛ת כָּל־שָׂרֵ֥י הַחֲיָלִ֖ים אֲשֶׁ֣ר אִתּ֑וֹ וַיִּשְׂמָֽחוּ׃
records.gloss: And it was as saw all the people who [were] with Ishmael Johanan son of Kareah and all [the] commanders of the forces who [were] with him, and they rejoiced.
pieces: When all the people Ishmael had with him saw Johanan son of Kareah and all the commanders of the forces with him, they were glad.

L.13: And it came about, when all the people who [were] with Ishmael saw Johanan son of Kareah and all the commanders of the forces who [were] with him, [that] they rejoiced.

R.13: When all the captives with Ishmael saw Johanan son of Kareah and the army commanders with him, they were overjoyed.

decisions.choice: the people who were with Ishmael: his captives
decisions.reason: These are the people he had taken from Mizpah (verses 10 and 14).

decisions.choice: captives; overjoyed (Readable)
decisions.reason: Readable says who the people were (m1) and uses a stronger word for their relief.

records.source: וַיָּסֹ֨בּוּ֙ כָּל־הָעָ֔ם אֲשֶׁר־שָׁבָ֥ה יִשְׁמָעֵ֖אל מִן־הַמִּצְפָּ֑ה וַיָּשֻׁ֨בוּ֙ וַיֵּ֣לְכ֔וּ אֶל־יֽוֹחָנָ֖ן בֶּן־קָרֵֽחַ׃
records.gloss: And turned around all the people whom had taken captive Ishmael from Mizpah, and they returned and went to Johanan son of Kareah.
pieces: All the people Ishmael had taken captive from Mizpah turned around and went back over to Johanan son of Kareah.

L.14: And all the people whom Ishmael had taken captive from Mizpah turned around and returned and went to Johanan son of Kareah.

R.14: All the people Ishmael had taken from Mizpah turned around and went back to Johanan son of Kareah.

decisions.choice: turned around, returned and went: they left Ishmael at once
decisions.reason: Three verbs in a row show the captives breaking away and going over to Johanan on the spot.

decisions.choice: went back over to (Balanced); went back to (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable join "returned and went" into one phrase.

records.source: וְיִשְׁמָעֵ֣אל בֶּן־נְתַנְיָ֗ה נִמְלַט֙ בִּשְׁמֹנָ֣ה אֲנָשִׁ֔ים מִפְּנֵ֖י יֽוֹחָנָ֑ן וַיֵּ֖לֶךְ אֶל־בְּנֵ֥י עַמּֽוֹן׃ס
records.gloss: And Ishmael son of Nethaniah escaped with eight men from [the] face of Johanan, and he went to [the] sons of Ammon.
pieces: But Ishmael son of Nethaniah got away from Johanan with eight men and went to the Ammonites.

L.15: But Ishmael son of Nethaniah escaped with eight men from before Johanan, and he went to the {{gender:children|sons}} of Ammon.

R.15: But Ishmael son of Nethaniah escaped from Johanan with eight of his men, and he went to the land of the Ammonites.

decisions.choice: with eight men: two fewer than the ten who came with him
decisions.reason: Ishmael had come with ten men (verse 1). The text does not say what became of the other two.

decisions.choice: from before Johanan: out of his reach
decisions.reason: "From the face of" Johanan means away from him, so that Johanan could not catch him.

decisions.choice: of his men; the land of (Readable)
decisions.reason: As in verse 10. Readable says the eight were his own men.

records.source: וַיִּקַּח֩ יוֹחָנָ֨ן בֶּן־קָרֵ֜חַ וְכָל־שָׂרֵ֧י הַחֲיָלִ֣ים אֲשֶׁר־אִתּ֗וֹ אֵ֣ת כָּל־שְׁאֵרִ֤ית הָעָם֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר הֵ֠שִׁיב מֵאֵ֨ת יִשְׁמָעֵ֤אל בֶּן־נְתַנְיָה֙ מִן־הַמִּצְפָּ֔ה אַחַ֣ר הִכָּ֔ה אֶת־גְּדַלְיָ֖ה בֶּן־אֲחִיקָ֑ם גְּבָרִ֞ים אַנְשֵׁ֣י הַמִּלְחָמָ֗ה וְנָשִׁ֤ים וְטַף֙ וְסָ֣רִסִ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֥ר הֵשִׁ֖יב מִגִּבְעֽוֹן׃
records.gloss: And took Johanan son of Kareah and all [the] commanders of the forces who [were] with him all [the] rest of the people whom he brought back from with Ishmael son of Nethaniah from Mizpah, after he struck Gedaliah son of Ahikam: men, men of the war, and women and little ones and eunuchs, whom he brought back from Gibeon.
pieces: Then Johanan son of Kareah and all the commanders of the forces with him took charge of all the rest of the people from Mizpah. Johanan had rescued them from Ishmael son of Nethaniah after the murder of Gedaliah son of Ahikam. They were fighting men, women, children and court officers, whom Johanan had brought back from Gibeon.

L.16: And Johanan son of Kareah and all the commanders of the forces who [were] with him took all the rest of the people whom he had brought back from Ishmael son of Nethaniah, from Mizpah, after he had struck down Gedaliah son of Ahikam: men, men of war, and women and little ones and eunuchs, whom he had brought back from Gibeon.

R.16: Johanan son of Kareah and all the army commanders with him then took charge of all the people from Mizpah who were left. Johanan had rescued them from Ishmael son of Nethaniah, who had killed Gedaliah son of Ahikam. There were soldiers, women, children and palace officials, and Johanan had brought them back from Gibeon.

decisions.choice: whom he had brought back ... after he had struck down Gedaliah: Johanan rescued them; Ishmael had killed Gedaliah
decisions.reason: The Hebrew uses "he" for both men without naming them. The one who brought the people back is Johanan (verse 14); the one who struck Gedaliah is Ishmael (verse 2). "From Mizpah" tells where the captives had come from.

decisions.choice: men, men of war: fighting men
decisions.reason: The two words stand side by side, "strong men" and "men of war", and together mean soldiers. Not all of Judah's soldiers had been killed in verse 3.

decisions.choice: eunuchs: royal court officials, perhaps castrated men
decisions.reason: As in 29:2 and 38:7, the word names a class of court officers. Such men often served the women of a royal household, and the king's daughters were among these people (verse 10).

decisions.choice: little ones: children
decisions.reason: The word means children too young to fend for themselves.

decisions.choice: eunuchs (Literal); court officers (Balanced); palace officials (Readable)
decisions.reason: As set for Jeremiah (and as 2 Kings 24:12), Literal keeps "eunuchs" and Balanced and Readable say what they were (m3): "court officers" and "palace officials". "Officials" alone is kept for *sar*.

decisions.choice: Johanan; Ishmael; the murder of Gedaliah (Balanced and Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name each man where the Hebrew says only "he" (m1), and split the long sentence.

records.source: וַיֵּלְכ֗וּ וַיֵּֽשְׁבוּ֙ בְּגֵר֣וּת כִּמְהָ֔ם אֲשֶׁר־אֵ֖צֶל בֵּ֣ית לָ֑חֶם לָלֶ֖כֶת לָב֥וֹא מִצְרָֽיִם׃
records.gloss: And they went and stayed in Geruth Chimham which [is] beside Bethlehem, to go to enter Egypt,
pieces: They set out and stopped at Geruth Chimham near Bethlehem, on their way to Egypt,

L.17: And they went and stayed at Geruth Chimham, which [is] beside Bethlehem, to go [and] enter Egypt,

R.17: They set out and stayed for a while at Geruth Chimham, near Bethlehem. They meant to go on from there to Egypt,

decisions.choice: Chimham: the name as it is read aloud
alternatives: the written form of the name
decisions.reason: The letters written in the Hebrew text spell the name a little differently, but the reading tradition marked in the margin says "Chimham", the name of a man known from 2 Samuel 19:38-41. That reading is followed here.

decisions.choice: Geruth Chimham: perhaps a lodging place named after Chimham
decisions.reason: "Geruth" may mean a place for travelers to stay. Chimham son of Barzillai went to Jerusalem with David (2 Samuel 19:38-41), and the place near Bethlehem may have been land given to his family. It is not mentioned anywhere else.

decisions.choice: to go and enter Egypt: their intention
decisions.reason: They had stopped on the road south toward Egypt and meant to go on. Before they went, they asked Jeremiah to pray for guidance (42:1-3).

decisions.choice: stopped (Balanced); stayed for a while (Readable); on their way (Balanced); meant to go on (Readable)
decisions.reason: The verb means they settled there for a time. Balanced and Readable make the purpose clause a plan for the journey ahead. All levels run on into verse 18 without a final stop.

records.source: מִפְּנֵי֙ הַכַּשְׂדִּ֔ים כִּ֥י יָרְא֖וּ מִפְּנֵיהֶ֑ם כִּֽי־הִכָּ֞ה יִשְׁמָעֵ֣אל בֶּן־נְתַנְיָ֗ה אֶת־גְּדַלְיָ֨הוּ֙ בֶּן־אֲחִיקָ֔ם אֲשֶׁר־הִפְקִ֥יד מֶֽלֶךְ־בָּבֶ֖ל בָּאָֽרֶץ׃ס
records.gloss: from [the] face of the Chaldeans, for they were afraid of them, for had struck Ishmael son of Nethaniah Gedaliah son of Ahikam, whom had appointed [the] king of Babylon over the land.
pieces: to escape the Chaldeans. They were afraid of them, because Ishmael son of Nethaniah had killed Gedaliah son of Ahikam, whom the king of Babylon had appointed governor of the land.

L.18: from before the Chaldeans, for they were afraid of them, because Ishmael son of Nethaniah had struck down Gedaliah son of Ahikam, whom the king of Babylon had appointed over the land.

R.18: to get away from the Babylonians. They were afraid of them because Ishmael son of Nethaniah had killed Gedaliah son of Ahikam, the man the king of Babylon had put in charge of the land.

decisions.choice: from the face of the Chaldeans: to get away from them
decisions.reason: They were going to Egypt to escape the Babylonians, who they feared would punish them all for the murder of the governor and the soldiers (2 Kings 25:26).

decisions.choice: whom the king of Babylon had appointed over the land: as verse 2
decisions.reason: The chapter closes with the words it used for Gedaliah at his death in verse 2. 2 Kings 25:26 sums up the flight in one verse.

decisions.choice: to escape (Balanced); to get away from the Babylonians (Readable); governor, put in charge of (as verse 2)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable explain the idiom (m1). Readable says "Babylonians" for the Chaldeans, as in Isaiah.
